title: Techniquely: Super Crunchy Buttermilk Fried Chicken — trim, brine, dredge + batter, fry at 340°F
summary: America’s Test Kitchen’s Techniquely episode walks through a method to achieve an exceptionally crispy, craggy fried chicken crust by pairing a dredge with a buttermilk-based batter, preceded by careful trimming, strategic breast-halving for even cooking, and a flexible brining step. The host trims fat and extra skin, cuts breasts on a diagonal for even pieces, and brines the chicken with salt (plus optional sugar, garlic powder, and cayenne) for flavor and juiciness. The coating uses a flour-cornstarch base with baking powder, seasoned to echo the brine, plus a viscous buttermilk batter. Frying is conducted at 340°F in two batches with safety-minded techniques (low dipping height, singleton hands for handling batter, and per-piece temperature checks). The video emphasizes carryover cooking, advising pulling darker meat at 160°F and breasts at 140°F to finish in residual heat, resulting in juicy meat and a crust that stays intact without dragging or greasing-up. The host also notes practical workflow tips (pan choice for dredge, over‑shooting heat for recovery, and avoiding a doughy undercoat) and points viewers to the ATK app for the full recipe and Cook Mode guidance.

sections.title: Trim, portioning, and brine prep
concepts: preparing mixed parts vs all-white or all-dark options
sections.description: The host begins with trimming excess fat and skin, discusses cutting breasts on an angle for even cooking and speedier doneness, and notes that different parts (drum, breast) may be used. Brining is introduced as a typical step for fried chicken to season and retain juiciness; the salt-to-water ratio is tuned to allow 2–24 hours of brining, with additional flavors (sugar, garlic powder, cayenne) included. The buttermilk is reserved for later use.

sections.title: Dredge and batter prep
sections.description: Brine notes lead into coating prep: flour forms the dredge base, cut with a substantial amount of cornstarch to reduce protein interaction and promote crispiness. Baking powder is added to lighten the crust. Flavorings (pepper, thyme, cayenne, garlic and onion powders) echo the brine. The dry mix is portioned to create a split between the dredge and the batter, with the dredge kept in a 13x9 pan for efficiency.

sections.title: Batter mixing, dredging, and frying setup
concepts: viscosity control for thin coating on a thick batter
coating chicken and dropping into oil
frying temperature strategy and batch management
sections.description: The batter is prepared with buttermilk to gain tang and moisture, but tests show a thick batter is undesirable; instead, a viscous, clingy batter is desired to avoid a doughy undercoat. The chicken is dredged and battered, then lowered into 340°F oil with a low, controlled drop to minimize splatter. Multiple safety tips are given: use one clean hand for handling battered pieces, don’t drop from height, and allow batches to cook independently. The host notes that oil temperature should overshoot before adding the chicken so the temperature recovers after loading.

sections.title: Finish, carryover, and wrap-up
concepts: carryover cooking and final internal temps
sections.description: The host explains carryover cooking: removing the chicken at 140°F for breasts and 160°F for dark meat to finish in residual heat, thanks to the crust acting as a heat blanket. The final product is described as juicy and well-seasoned with a craggy, crunchy crust. The video ends with a call to use the ATK app for the full recipe and Cook Mode guidance.
